name: screening-degraded
rationale: Readiness Epic D's graceful-degradation claim, measured rather than asserted: an intelligence that is slow, not down, while customers screen withdrawals. Warmup (60s) runs healthy so the subject builds what production has when an incident starts -- snapshots for the counterparties in play, a synced sanctions view, latency history. Then 300ms is added to every intelligence response for the measurement window: above the default fresh budget ceiling (150ms), below the hard deadline (500ms), so the stale path is what is exercised and, after SCREENING_BREAKER_FAILURE_THRESHOLD slow reads, the open breaker. 50 screening qps over a 500-address pool: counterparties repeat (warmup screens each ~6 times), which is what makes a snapshot exist; a pool of fresh addresses would measure fail-closed only. The chain runs at 4 blocks/s fully alerting so the fast-path gates collect their 500 samples and the run is not inconclusive for a reason unrelated to screening. Judged on screen_p50 and screen_p99 over the degraded window (the breaker is what keeps p50 under 100ms once open), and screen_failed_closed (<= 1% 502s); screen_stale_share is reported beside them.
